patch_description: The current best score (0.99) corresponds to a squared ratio of ~0.2397, essentially at the reference 0.24 but not above it. The annealing ladder stops at T=0.002, so the smoothed min/max ratio still slightly differs from the exact ratio dmin/dmax; the optimizer can terminate before the exact binding constraints (closest and farthest pairs) are fully balanced. The most direct way to squeeze out the remaining gap is a final low-temperature polish stage run only on the best configuration found so far: continue the annealing ladder down to T=0.0008 and 0.0003 with tighter L-BFGS-B tolerances, and wrap it in a few small-magnitude perturbation restarts (magnitude ~0.004-0.01, far smaller than the 0.02+ used in the existing restarts, so we stay in the basin of the good optimum while escaping tiny numerical plateaus). Each candidate is scored with the exact `ratio()`, and the best is kept. This is cheap (only a handful of extra L-BFGS-B runs on 42 variables), preserves the existing structure, and directly targets the metric the evaluator computes — the exact dmin/dmax, not the smoothed surrogate.
